messages:
Ryan: Kicking off a shadow run — trying an AWQ int4 bring-up with a concat-prefix warmstart + continuous batching. Want to validate accuracy delta vs fp8/GPTQ and watch KV cache warmup behavior. Please follow along and drop observations.
Maria: Can you paste the exact runtime config you used? especially batching window, prefetch TTL and concat warmstart flag.
Ryan: Config we used for the first pass:
```
model: my-candidate-awq-int4
batching: {window_ms: 30, max_batch_tokens: 4096}
prefetch: {enabled: true, ttl_ms: 120000}
kv_cache: {strategy: concat-warmstart, max_entries: 20000}
quant: {type: awq, bits: 4}
shadow: true
```
Sam: First-pass metrics from the shadow run (100k requests sampled):
- EM delta vs baseline fp16: -2.8% absolute
- Per-token perplexity change: +0.12
- Latency p50/p95: 18ms / 94ms (baseline fp16 16ms / 80ms)
- KV cache hit rate after 5min: 62% (baseline warmstart fp8: 74%)
- Cost per token estimate: ~0.36x of fp16
Jin: Interesting — the concat-warmstart seems to reduce effective cache reuse for short prefixes. I suspect collision/overlap logic in concat keys. Can you dump a few cache keys that missed?
Ryan: Pasting a couple of misses (sanitized):
```
miss: prefix_hash=0x8fa3, seq=0..32, key_len=38
miss: prefix_hash=0x8fa3, seq=1..33, key_len=37
hit: prefix_hash=0xa12b, seq=0..25, key_len=26
```
Lisa: That pattern looks like off-by-one sequence normalization — concat-warmstart appends a control token which shifts key boundaries. GPTQ and fp8 variants normalize before hashing which AWQ path might not be doing.
Sam: We also saw slightly higher tail because when concat-warmstart misses, the runtime falls back to a full decode path and that blows up p95 for a subset of requests.
Maria: Can we try two quick experiments:
1) normalize keys in AWQ path before hashing (strip control token) — low-risk.
2) bump batching window to 50ms to let more KV hits accumulate.
Jin: Agreed. I'll patch key normalization and run a micro-benchmark. Patch diff:
```
- cache_key = hash(prefix + control_token)
+ cache_key = hash(normalize(prefix) + control_token_stripped)
```
infra-bot: deploy started: eng-ml/kv-keynorm/2024-11-08T09:12:13Z -> canary=5 pods
Lisa: If we normalize, we should also check for unintended aliasing across prompt templates. Add a template id salt if necessary.
Sam: Ran the normalized-key micro run: cache hit jumped from 62% -> 71% and p95 dropped to 82ms. EM delta improved to -1.6% vs fp16 on the same sample.
eval-bot: Eval harness results (balanced QA set, 10k examples): AWQ-int4 (with key-norm) EM -1.5% vs fp16, F1 -0.9 pts. FP8 baseline EM -0.4%.
Ryan: That narrows the accuracy gap but still nontrivial. Maria, can you queue a full-night A/B: AWQ-int4(key-norm, concat-warmstart), FP8 (warmstart normalized), and GPTQ-int8 (no concat) with same batching windows? Also capture prefix length distribution and per-route tail latency.
Maria: Yep — scheduling now, will run three shadow cohorts overnight and collect per-route metrics + sample outputs for eval.
Jin: Also instrument kv-cache to record prefix collision rate and a small histogram of key_len distribution. Helpful snippet:
```
metrics.kv_collision_total.inc()
metrics.kv_keylen_hist.observe(len(key))
```
Lisa: For deployment profiles, remember Dedicated customers may tune ttl_ms much higher; we should test 2min vs 10min prefetch TTLs because AWQ's reduced model size might make longer TTL more attractive.
Sam: Quick note — continuous batching window interacts weirdly: at 30ms we saw more misses (less time to aggregate) but lower mean latency; 50ms improved hits but increased mean. There will be a cost/latency tradeoff depending on SLO.
Ryan: Good observation. We'll capture cost-per-req vs p95 curves for window_ms in [10,20,30,50,80]. Maria add that to the job.
Maria: Added. Running now. ETA full results tomorrow 10am PT.
Lisa: Minor: capture the request shape (prompt_len, gen_len) — AWQ accuracy seems prompt-length sensitive in small sample.
Ryan: Thanks everyone. TL;DR: AWQ-int4 is promising on cost, had initial KV keying bug with concat-warmstart causing misses. Key normalization + small batching/window tuning recovered most of the gap. Overnight A/B + TTL sweep will decide whether AWQ-int4 can be default in dedicated/dedicated-shadow profiles.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Jin: ping me once overnight results land, I'll run deeper kv-key collision analysis.
Maria: Will post the full CSV + example failures to the thread when done.
Lisa: If overnight looks good, we can plan a limited canary (10% traffic) on a non-critical route next week.
Ryan: Perfect. Closing for now, will follow up with results."
